en: Udāna 6.1 Āyusaṅkhārossajjanasutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the Gabled Hall.
Then, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, the Blessed One entered Vesālī for alms.
Having walked for alms in Vesālī and returned from his almsround after the meal, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
“Take your sitting mat, Ānanda;
we will go to the Cāpāla Shrine for the day’s rest.
“Very well, Bhante,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One, and taking his sitting mat, he followed closely behind the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One approached the Cāpāla Shrine; having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat.
Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
“Delightful, Ānanda, is Vesālī; delightful is the Udena Shrine; delightful is the Gotamaka Shrine.”
The Sattamba Cetiya is delightful; the Bahuputta Cetiya is delightful; the Sārandada Cetiya is delightful;
the Cāpāla Cetiya is delightful.

Ānanda, whoever has developed, cultivated, mastered, made a basis for, established, familiarized, and properly undertaken the four bases of psychic power—should he so desire, he could remain for an eon or for the remainder of an eon.
“Ānanda, the four bases of psychic power have been developed, cultivated, made a vehicle, made a foundation, established, consolidated, and properly undertaken by the Tathāgata.
If he so desired, Ānanda, the Tathāgata could remain for an eon, or for the remainder of an eon.
Yet even when such a gross sign was being made manifest and such a gross indication was being given, the Venerable Ānanda was unable to penetrate it.
He did not entreat the Blessed One, saying:

“Venerable sir, let the Blessed One remain for an eon; let the Sugata remain for an eon for the welfare of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans,” because his mind was obsessed by Māra.
A second time also... [as before]...
A third time, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
“Delightful, Ānanda, is Vesālī; delightful is the Udena Shrine; delightful is the Gotamaka Shrine;
delightful is the Sattamba Shrine; delightful is the Bahuputta Shrine; delightful is the Sārandada Shrine.”
The Cāpāla Shrine is beautiful.

Ānanda, whoever has developed, cultivated, mastered, established, consolidated, and properly undertaken the four bases for psychic power could, if they so desired, remain for an eon or for the remainder of an eon.
Now, Ānanda, the Tathāgata has indeed developed, cultivated, mastered, and established the four bases for psychic power.
“Practiced, cultivated, and well-undertaken. If he so desired, Ānanda, the Tathāgata could remain for an eon, or for the remainder of an eon.
Even though such a broad hint was given by the Blessed One, and such a broad indication was made, the Venerable Ānanda was unable to penetrate it;
he did not entreat the Blessed One:

“May the Blessed One remain, venerable sir, for an eon; may the Sugata remain for an eon for the welfare of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans,” said he whose mind was obsessed by Māra.
Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
“Go, Ānanda, now is the time as you deem fit.”

“Yes, Bhante,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. He rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, and keeping him to his right, sat down at the foot of a certain tree not far away.

Then, not long after the Venerable Ānanda had departed, Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One; having approached, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, Māra the Evil One said this to the Blessed One:
“May the Blessed One now attain final nibbāna, venerable sir; may the Sugata now attain final nibbāna. Now is the time for the Blessed One’s final nibbāna, venerable sir.
For this word was indeed spoken by the Blessed One:
‘Evil One, I shall not attain final nibbāna as long as my bhikkhu disciples have not become accomplished, trained, and proficient...’”
They will be disciplined, confident, learned, bearers of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing with proper conduct, and living according to the Dhamma;
having mastered their own teacher’s tradition, they will explain, teach, proclaim, establish, reveal, analyze, and clarify it,
and they will thoroughly refute the doctrines of others that have arisen by means of the Dhamma.
‘Having restrained them, they will teach the Dhamma with its wonders. But now, Bhante,
the bhikkhus who are the Blessed One’s disciples are competent, disciplined, confident, learned, bearers of the Dhamma,
practitioners of the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, practitioners of the proper way, followers of the Dhamma, and maintainers of their own teacher’s tradition.
Having mastered them, they declare, teach, lay down, establish, reveal, analyze, and clarify them.
Having thoroughly refuted the doctrines of others with reasoned arguments, they teach the Dhamma accompanied by miracles.
"May the Blessed One now attain final Nibbāna; may the Sugata now attain final Nibbāna; the time for the Blessed One’s final Nibbāna has now come, venerable sir."
Furthermore, Bhante, this word was spoken by the Blessed One: “Evil One,
I shall not attain final nibbāna as long as my bhikkhunīs have not become disciples who are proficient,
disciplined, confident, learned, bearers of the Dhamma, practitioners of the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, practitioners of the proper way, and followers of the Dhamma.”
‘Having mastered their own teacher’s tradition, they will declare it, teach it, lay it down, establish it,
reveal it, analyze it, and make it clear; and having thoroughly refuted with reasoned arguments the doctrines of others that have arisen,
they will teach the Dhamma accompanied by miracles.’”
But now, Bhante, the bhikkhunīs who are the Blessed One’s disciples— distinguished, disciplined, confident, learned, bearers of the Dhamma,
practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing with proper conduct, walking according to the Dhamma,
having mastered their own teacher’s instruction— are explaining, teaching, proclaiming, establishing, revealing, analyzing, and making clear [the Dhamma].
Having thoroughly refuted with reasoned argument any arisen doctrine of others, they teach the Dhamma accompanied by miracles.
"Venerable sir, let the Blessed One now attain final Nibbāna; let the Sugata now attain final Nibbāna. Now is the time, venerable sir, for the Blessed One’s final Nibbāna.
For this word, venerable sir, has been spoken by the Blessed One:"
“Evil One, I shall not attain final nibbāna as long as my lay followers have not become disciples who are proficient,
disciplined, confident, learned, bearers of the Dhamma, practitioners of the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, practitioners of the proper way, and followers of the Dhamma; who,
having mastered their own teacher’s tradition, will declare it, teach it, lay it out, and establish it.”
‘They will reveal, analyze, and clarify [the Dhamma]; having well-refuted with reasoned argument any opposing doctrines that have arisen, they will teach the Dhamma accompanied by miracles.
And now, Bhante, the lay followers of the Blessed One are discerning, disciplined, confident, and learned.
They are bearers of the Dhamma, practitioners of the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, practitioners of proper conduct, and followers of the Dhamma.
Having mastered their own teacher’s tradition, they declare it, teach it, lay it out, establish it, reveal it, analyze it, and make it clear.
Having well refuted the doctrines of others that have arisen by means of the Dhamma, they teach the Dhamma accompanied by miracles.
“May the Blessed One now attain final Nibbāna, venerable sir; may the Sugata now attain final Nibbāna. Now is the time for the Blessed One’s final Nibbāna, venerable sir.
For this word was indeed spoken by the Blessed One:
‘Evil One, I shall not attain final Nibbāna until my female lay disciples have become accomplished...’”
Disciplined, confident, learned, bearers of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing with proper conduct, walking according to the Dhamma,
having mastered their own teacher’s tradition, they will explain, teach, proclaim, establish, reveal, analyze, and clarify it;
and they will thoroughly refute, with reasoned argument, the doctrines of others that have arisen.
‘Having restrained them, they will teach the Dhamma with its wonders. But now, Bhante,
there are female lay disciples who are the Blessed One’s disciples— discerning, disciplined, confident, learned, bearers of the Dhamma,
practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing with proper conduct, walking according to the Dhamma, and maintaining their own teacher’s tradition.
Having mastered them, they declare, teach, lay down, establish, reveal, analyze, and clarify them.
Having thoroughly refuted the doctrines of others with reasoned arguments, they teach the Dhamma accompanied by miracles.
"Venerable sir, let the Blessed One now attain final Nibbāna; let the Sugata now attain final Nibbāna. Now is the time for the Blessed One’s final Nibbāna."
“Indeed, Bhante, this was spoken by the Blessed One:
‘Evil One, I will not attain final nibbāna until this holy life has become successful, prosperous, widespread, popular, and well-proclaimed among gods and humans.
And now, Bhante, the Blessed One’s holy life has indeed become successful, prosperous, widespread, popular, and well-proclaimed among gods and humans.”
“Venerable sir, let the Blessed One now attain final nibbāna; let the Sublime One now attain final nibbāna. Now is the time for the Blessed One’s final nibbāna.
When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to Māra the Evil One:
“Be at ease, Evil One. The Tathāgata’s final nibbāna will not be long delayed.”
"Three months from now, the Tathāgata will attain final nibbāna.
Then, at the Cāpāla Shrine, the Blessed One—mindful and clearly comprehending—relinquished the life-force.
And when the Blessed One had relinquished the life-force, there was a great earthquake, terrifying and hair-raising, and the divine drums resounded.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“The Sage has relinquished both the measurable and the immeasurable, the source of becoming, and the formative activity of existence.”
Delighting in the internal, composed in mind,
he has shattered his own rebirth like a coat of mail. Thus ends the first [verse].
